text: It may be objected that the chapter observes only the severe economy of ancient narrative, which rarely reports the feelings of persons and never explains either their feelings or their motives; and this may, in part, be true. But the narrator can report feeling when he will: Esau cries out, Jacob is afraid, Joseph weeps. The reticence here, therefore, is chosen, and the narrator is conscious of his choice; in this voice restraint functions as accusation in Genesis 22.
